ruling_text:
Kalos Specialized Services, Inc v Charis Wallace

Tentative Ruling:

To deny, without prejudice.

If oral argument is timely requested, such argument will be entertained on Friday,
March 27, 2026, at 9:00 a.m., in Department 501.
Explanation:

Plaintiff Ray Thacker (“plaintiff”) moves the court for an order verifying the current
and actual military status of defendant Jose D. Anguiano (“defendant”). Plaintiff brings
this motion under California Military and Veterans Code section 401 and the
Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (“SCRA”), 50 U.S.C. section 3931. However, the court is
unaware how each of these code sections confers the authority to “verify” a party’s
military status, nor how they allow the court to make the orders and directives requested
by plaintiff. Plaintiff refers to these laws, but fails to cite to the portions authorizing the
court to grant the relief requested.

Further, plaintiff offers no evidence to support granting the motion. Plaintiff merely
contends that there is “uncertainty” that defendant is actively serving in the military, but
fails to provide any supporting evidence. The entirety of plaintiff’s motion appears to be
based in speculation.

Due to the lack of authority and evidence, the court intends to deny the motion,
without prejudice.

Pursuant to California Rules of Court, rule 3.1312(a), and Code of Civil Procedure
section 1019.5, subdivision (a), no further written order is necessary. The minute order
adopting this tentative ruling will serve as the order of the court and service by the clerk
will constitute notice of the order.
